Container.Name: circuit-breaker-tracker
Container.Overview:
Recreate your electrical panels, label every breaker and what it serves, share them with scoped access, and print panel directories.
The app runs as user 1000 inside the container. Before the first start, make the appdata folder writable for it, from the Unraid terminal: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/circuit-breaker-tracker && chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/circuit-breaker-tracker
Then open the web UI and create the first admin account on the setup screen.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: Port the web UI listens on. With host networking this must be free on the server. If you change it, open the UI at that port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Holds the database (breakers.db). Must be owned by 1000:1000 (see Overview).

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address people use to reach the app, e.g. https://breakers.example.com or http://192.168.1.10:2757. Used in invite links; required for Microsoft sign-in.

Config.Name: Behind a reverse proxy
Config.Description: Set to true when Nginx Proxy Manager, SWAG, Caddy or Traefik sits in front of the app.

Config.Name: First admin username
Config.Description: Optional. Creates the first admin at startup instead of using the setup screen. Ignored once any user exists.

Config.Name: First admin password
Config.Description: Optional, with the username above. At least 10 characters.

Config.Name: Microsoft / OIDC issuer
Config.Description: Optional single sign-on, e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT-ID/v2.0. Needs Public URL. Redirect URI to register: PUBLIC_URL/api/auth/oidc/callback

Config.Name: OIDC client ID
Config.Description: Application (client) ID from the app registration.

Config.Name: OIDC client secret
Config.Description: Client secret value from the app registration.

Config.Name: SSO button text
Config.Description: Text on the single sign-on button.
